review_focus.jax_scan_logic: PASS — carry has 17 elements (added slot_pnl), init_carry correctly initializes the new array, step() and final_carry unpack all 17 elements. Order of operations is correct: release (with PnL credit) → position sizing (using post-release equity) → entry (store PnL in slot, no equity update) → Sortino stat compute (with post-release equity).
review_focus.slot_management: PASS — _jax_open_slot uses can_open = can_trade & has_empty mask; when no empty slot, can_open is False and slot_release/slot_pnl/open_exposure are unchanged. Final release block after scan handles positions that never release within the loop (release_idx >= N).

edge_cases.no_slots_free: PASS — _jax_open_slot gates updates with can_open mask; signal still counts as executed if can_trade, but slot arrays are unchanged and exposure not increased.
edge_cases.all_slots_occupied: PASS — same as above; subsequent signals on same row are correctly skipped from slot update.
edge_cases.final_unreleased_positions: PASS — block after lax.scan computes remaining_pnl, remaining_wins/losses/gp/gl from active slot_pnl, and applies them to equity, peak, max_dd, wins, losses, gross_profit, gross_loss. This is correct because PnL was stored at entry and is now realized.
edge_cases.account_ruined: PASS — new_ruined uses post-release equity (new_equity = equity + equity_delta), matching CPU engine's `if equity <= 0: break` after release.

review_focus.numerical_stability: PASS — _JXF (float32 by default) accumulations are bounded by test tolerances (±1% return, ±5% DD/Sortino). jnp.sum over slot_pnl is correct. The fix doesn't introduce additional accumulations compared to the old code (in fact, fewer because PnL is summed once at release instead of added at entry).
review_focus.sortino_consistency: PASS — The spec text said Sortino should accumulate at release, but the implementer correctly identified that the CPU engine actually computes trade_ret = net_pnl / equity AFTER releases (so equity already reflects released PnL). The GPU code matches this: trade_ret = net_pnl / new_equity where new_equity is post-release. The docstring in _jax_release_open_slots explicitly documents this rationale.
review_focus.regression_check_zero_signal: PASS — _zero_signal_result_row is unchanged and only used when signal_mask is all-False (no scan path).
review_focus.regression_check_fast_reject: PASS — _fast_reject_result_rows is unchanged and only used when raw_signal_count < trade_floor (no scan path).
review_focus.regression_check_simulate_rule_set: PASS — CPU delegation path is unchanged.
review_focus.test_coverage: ADEQUATE — test_gpu_cpu_return_parity covers 10 random chromosomes, binary+signed features, 120-row multi-symbol dataset, with tolerances matching acceptance criteria. Covers all 6 required metrics. Could be expanded to short direction and longer data, but is sufficient for the fix's primary goal.

key_observations: The slot_pnl approach is the cleanest way to parallelize the CPU engine's sequential release loop. Each slot independently holds its own PnL, and release is a single jnp.where mask sum — no per-slot Python branching.
Final release is critical and correctly implemented: positions opened near the end of the data whose release_index >= N would otherwise be lost. The block credits PnL and updates all relevant stats.
The spec deviation on Sortino is actually a CORRECT deviation: matching CPU engine behavior is more important than literal spec text. The implementer's note in the docstring makes this clear.
Float32 vs float64 drift is bounded by the test tolerances. The fix doesn't worsen this — slot_pnl is a single value per slot, summed at release, which is the same precision as the old code.
No code-smell or dead code: old entry-time equity updates were cleanly removed; no commented-out leftovers; carry structure is well-organized with consistent naming.
Reuse of _zero_signal_result_row, _fast_reject_result_rows, and CPU delegation path is preserved (no regression).
minor_observations: Test could be strengthened by also testing 'short' direction (not just 'long') and larger chromosomes (3+ features). However, this is a test quality nitpick, not a blocker — the spec acceptance criteria are met.
The docstring in _jax_release_open_slots could mention the `account_ruined` interaction, but this is also fine because the post-step check is documented elsewhere.
A targeted unit test specifically for the final-release edge case (positions opened in last 288 bars) would be valuable to lock in behavior, but the parity test exercises this implicitly.
verdict_reasoning: The implementation correctly defers PnL credit to release time, matching the CPU engine's behavior. All edge cases (no slots free, final unreleased positions, account_ruined) are handled. The Sortino stat deviation from the spec text is a correct implementation detail that matches the actual CPU engine. The new parity test covers the 6 required metrics within the specified tolerances. All 61 existing GPU engine tests still pass. No regressions in non-scan code paths (_zero_signal_result_row, _fast_reject_result_rows, CPU delegation). The fix is clean, minimal, and well-documented.
recommendation: APPROVED. Ready to merge to main after Task 1 (already merged). No blocking issues.
